# Alignment with TRY

[TRY](https://www.try-db.org/) is the plant trait database run by the Max Planck
Institute for Biogeochemistry. It defines traits by name and number, such as trait 14,
*Leaf nitrogen (N) content per leaf dry mass*. This page maps the 2661 TRY traits
to BERVO. The work is tracked in
[issue #27](https://github.com/bioepic-data/bervo/issues/27) and is done in slices. The
first slice was the map itself. The second added terms for the traits used by the
[plant-functional-traits](https://github.com/bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits)
schema. The third added the leaf economics and photosynthesis traits: leaf phosphorus,
N:P ratios, photosynthetic and dark respiration rates, Vcmax, Jmax, stomatal conductance,
leaf lifespan, thickness, tissue density, dry mass and phenology. The fourth added the
organ and status concepts the `broader` rows named but BERVO lacked, such as twig, bark,
coarse woody debris and senescent vegetation. The fifth added plant hydraulics and water
relations: xylem vulnerability to embolism, leaf water potentials, hydraulic conductance and
conductivity, the Huber value and xylem conduit size. The sixth added root traits: dry
matter content, lignin content, respiration rate, branching ratio, root tip abundance,
lifespan, rooting depth and mycorrhizal colonization, with the root to shoot ratio. The
seventh added seed, fruit and dispersal traits: seed and diaspore dimensions, seed fresh
mass, terminal velocity, oil and protein content, seeds per fruit, dispersal distance,
fruit size and mass, and the base temperature and water potential for germination. The
eighth added stem, wood and bark traits: bark thickness and density, with inner and outer
bark, stem dry matter content, respiration rate and specific length, tree ring width, stem
hydraulic conductivity, conduit lumen area and length, and sapwood area. The ninth added
root traits that TRY also splits into coarse, fine, absorptive and transport roots:
non-structural carbohydrate and starch content, stele diameter, cortex thickness, conduit
diameter, specific root area and turnover rate, with organ dry mass per ground area
mapped to the biomass terms. The tenth added potassium, calcium and magnesium content
for any plant tissue, mapped the carbon, nitrogen and oxygen isotope signatures of plant
organs to the existing isotope delta terms and the oxygen and hydrogen signatures of
sapwood water to the water delta terms, and finished the woody organ biomass traits. The
eleventh added the content of eleven more elements for any plant tissue (S, Na, Mn, Fe,
Zn, Cu, Al, Ni, Si, B and Mo) and the most used leaf traits: stomatal density, leaf
length and width, petiole length, fresh mass, chlorophyll, lignin, cellulose,
non-structural carbohydrate and starch content, vein density, photosynthetic nitrogen and
water use efficiency, transpiration rate and leaf area ratio. Still to come are the value
lists of the categorical traits (woodiness, growth form, leaf type, leaf phenology) and
terms for the gaps listed here.

## Sources

| Source | Revision | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `try_traits.csv`, attached to issue #27 | attached 2026-01-29, fetched 2026-10-22 | The 2661 TRY traits, as `trait_id` and `trait_name` only. It is byte-identical to `data/try_traits.csv` in plant-functional-traits. |
| [`bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits`](https://github.com/bioepic-data/plant-functional-traits), `src/plant_functional_traits/schema/plant_functional_traits.yaml` | `d083f09` | Which TRY traits the harmonized schema uses, in the `pft_slot` column |

The TRY list has no units, definitions or value types. A term added from it takes those
from the TRY data release documentation or from the literature the trait comes from, not
from the list. TRY cuts trait names at 100 characters, so a few end mid-word; they are
kept as given. Eleven names occur twice under different IDs, such as 456 and 1527, both
*Coarse root carbon (C) content per coarse root dry mass*. The map keeps both IDs and
points them at the same term.

## The map

The map is `src/scripts/try/try_alignment.tsv`, written by
`src/scripts/build_try_alignment.py`, one row per TRY trait:

| Column | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `trait_id`, `trait_name` | as in TRY |
| `group` | the organ or theme, used to plan slices |
| `status` | one of the five below |
| `bervo_id` | the BERVO term, for `match`, `broader` and `related` |
| `pft_slot` | the plant-functional-traits schema slot the trait feeds, if any |
| `note` | why a `related` term is not the same quantity, or another caveat |

| Status | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `match` | A BERVO term is the same quantity. |
| `broader` | A general BERVO term covers the trait, with what narrows it, such as an organ, a status or a time of day, in `contexts`. For example, *Stem nitrogen (N) content per stem dry mass* is `Plant tissue nitrogen content` with `Stem` in `contexts`. |
| `related` | A BERVO term is close but is not the same quantity, such as a reciprocal, a different normalisation, or an EcoSIM parameter defined differently. A term for the TRY trait is still needed. |
| `gap` | BERVO has no term. |
| `species_attribute` | The trait records where a species occurs, its habitat or indicator values, its legal status, its phylogeny or its uses, or it names a species, such as the dominant species of a plot or the herbivores of a leaf, rather than recording a property of a plant. These are set aside for a decision on scope, not rejected. |

Groups and the `species_attribute` status are assigned by rules on the trait name, which
were checked by hand. The C/N and N/P rows in `broader` are assigned the same way, as
are the element contents per unit dry mass for C, N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Na, Mn, Fe, Zn,
Cu, Al, Ni, Si, B and Mo. Root contents per unit of soil mass and root microbial biomass
were excluded from them, since neither is the content of a plant tissue. Every `match`
and `related` row was assigned by hand.

A `broader` row is recorded with a concept for what narrows it in `contexts`: an organ, a
status such as senescent, or a time of day such as predawn. Where the trait name says which, the row's `note` names the concept, such as *Twig goes in
contexts.* Some TRY organs map to a BERVO concept with another name: a *belowground plant
organ* is `Belowground plant material`, a *reproductive organ* is `Reproductive
structure`, and *senescent* leaves take `Senescent vegetation`.

## When an EcoSIM term is a match

Many BERVO plant terms are EcoSIM parameters with `Plant functional type` in `contexts`.
Such a term is a `match` when it is the same quantity, as `Seed length` and `Root
porosity` are. A value for a plant functional type is the trait's value for that type, as
a TRY species mean is the trait's value for a species, and BERVO keeps one term per
quantity whoever reports it. An EcoSIM variable resolved over something else, such as a
branch, a node or a grid cell, measures a different thing and is `related`: `Leaf number`
counts the leaves on a branch, not on a plant, and `Leaf area` is a grid-cell total.

## How the alignment is recorded on a term

- A `match` term records the ID in its `Comment` as `TRY trait ID: 14.`, or
  `TRY trait IDs: 3108, 3109.` when several TRY traits are the same quantity.
- A `broader` term records the IDs as `TRY traits mapped here, with what narrows each one in
  contexts: 80, 406.`, following the pattern of the AmeriFlux BADM fields mapped to the same
  terms.
- A `match` term takes the TRY trait name as a `Related Synonyms` value, unless the name is
  already its label, is a label or synonym of another term, or is cut off at 100
  characters in the TRY list. TRY's own abbreviations,
  such as SLA, LDMC and SSD, go in `Exact Synonyms`.
- TRY has no registered prefix, and its trait pages have no stable URL, so there is no
  `TRY:` cross-reference in `DbXrefs`.

`just try-doc` rebuilds this page, and it fails if the map and the `Comment` sentences
disagree. `tests/test_try_alignment.py` runs it.

## The plant-functional-traits schema

The schema harmonizes TRY, AusTraits and fine-root trait data into one record per taxon.
It is preliminary, so these rows are where the next slice starts, not the limit of it.
Several of its TRY columns are aggregates of more than one TRY trait. Leaf area, for
example, is spread over seven traits that differ in how a compound leaf and its petiole
are counted, so each slot lists every trait it may draw on. The `leaf_mass_per_area`
slot has no row: TRY has no trait of that name, since LMA is the reciprocal of SLA, and
BERVO already has `Leaf mass per area` (`BERVO:0002185`).
